A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Puppet-Master by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, architectural ablations, and data-curation experiments in Section 5 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons and qualitative analyses in Figures 4 and 8–10.

M1.justification: The backbone, drag modulation, all-to-first attention, and curation pipeline are retained. However, Section 3.2 changes the stated cross-attention pairs from 1+Kmax with zero padding to 1+K, without clarifying whether the implementation changed or the description merely omits padding.

E1.justification: The training datasets and two quantitative benchmarks remain. v2 adds explicit qualitative scenarios involving complex backgrounds and unsuitable global-motion drags (Appendix E, Figures 9–10). Fauna is no longer named, but retained animal examples prevent concluding that its represented coverage was removed.

E2.justification: v2 adds Image Conductor to both quantitative benchmarks in Table 1 and to qualitative comparisons, and adds a qualitative Sora comparison in Figure 4. DragNUWA, DragAnything, and both DragAPart checkpoints remain. Image Conductor was already cited in v1 but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 576×576 control for the previously discussed 256×256 SVD test, Image Conductor preprocessing, and image/text prompting for Sora. SVD’s stated pretraining resolution changes from 576×320 to 1024×576, without establishing reruns. Appendix C.2 contradicts itself about generating 14 frames directly versus truncating 16 frames for Image Conductor. The metric description also changes from RMSE to L2 distance without clarifying normalization.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially broadens analysis with seed and drag variation, global-motion failures, coordinated-part failures, and complex-background case studies. Figure 8 extends v1’s resolution-failure observation with a higher-resolution comparison. Original architectural and data-curation ablations remain; the latter moves from Section 5.3 to Appendix B.2.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly identifies Figure 9(a–b) as outputs from different random seeds with identical image and drag conditioning. This is limited qualitative seed reporting; neither version reports benchmark run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Image Conductor results, including PSNR 9.20 on Drag-a-Move and 8.02 on Human3.6M. New qualitative results include Sora’s unsuccessful example, motion diversity, part-disappearance failures, and complex-background outputs. Shared Table 1 scores and Tables 2–3 results remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding in Table 2.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, modulation and all-to-first attention equations, and Appendix A’s formal drag encoding are retained. Changes to equation numbering, batch-dimension notation, and explicit function arguments do not constitute new mathematical reasoning. Neither version adds theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim drag-controlled part-level video generation, architectural conditioning improvements, curated synthetic animation data, and zero-shot generalization to real images. v2’s foundation-model framing elaborates the universal motion-model motivation already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability limits absent from v1: unsuitable global-motion prompts, disappearing parts during coordinated motion, color mismatch, flicker, and complex-background limitations (Appendix E). Section 3.3 also replaces the resolution-only culprit assertion with a hypothesis involving both resolution and visual-content mismatch. Appendix B.2 narrows the data-quality interpretation to this fine-tuning setting.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 100 evaluation videos per quantitative benchmark, identifies baseline backbones and training datasets, and supplies category prompts and the full Sora prompt. Core model training, hardware, and inference details remain. However, v1’s explicit statement that architectural ablations omit classifier-free guidance disappears.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Cosmos, Genie 2, Sora, and Motion Prompting, while removing several adaptive-conditioning references and the MagicPony/Fauna citations. These update the world-model context and supporting literature without fundamentally changing the paper’s research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and method explanations undergo substantial rewriting. Evaluation settings receive a dedicated subsection, data-curation analysis moves into Appendix B.2, and the appendices gain a more detailed hierarchy. The retained flow-error metric is renamed Motion Error.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, introduces a new opening montage, and substantially rebuilds the qualitative comparison and example figures. Table 1 gains baseline-information columns and colored rankings. Figure 6 is reduced and rearranged, Figure 7 and Table 3 move to the appendix, and Figures 8–10 are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical context and transparency through additional comparisons and concrete demonstrations of variability, background handling, and failures, while preserving the original quantitative evidence. These gains are mostly qualitative. Conflicting Image Conductor frame-selection descriptions and the lost ablation-guidance clarification limit reproducibility, but the expanded evidence and explicit applicability boundaries support a modest net improvement.
